assign.brief: The owner, on /framework/ux/Dictate/, reported a layout bug in the mobile rail's AI pop-up chat UI (ext/drawer/rail.js's mobile assistant, built on ux/Dictate's Widget/Chat): 'When I make it full screen, the scrollable text area is not filling the available space properly. And then there's a void underneath the buttons. Well, I guess the text area is growing, and so...' (trailed off). Likely cause: the chat thread's scroll container isn't sized to fill the fullscreen height (flex/height not propagated), and growth of the composer textarea is shrinking/leaving a gap rather than the thread area reflowing to fill it. Reproduce the mobile rail chat in fullscreen (phone width, use the site shot/eval tools), find the root CSS/layout cause in ext/drawer/ and ext/Chat/ext/Dictate's Widget, fix it, verify at phone width with a screenshot, and land the task per finish-task.

decision.what: Root cause found by reading code (ext/drawer/rail.js, rail.css, ux/Dictate/Widget.js, Widget.css): Widget.css caps .ux-dictate-widget-thread at max-block-size: 22em, sized for a standalone widget on a normal page. rail.css already turns the CARD's own max-block-size off inside the fullscreen sheet (.ux-dictate-widget-card { max-block-size: none }) so the card fills the screen, but never turned off the THREAD's own separate 22em cap one level deeper -- rail.css's own comment right above that override literally says the thread should get the same nested-flex treatment, it just never actually got it. In fullscreen (100dvh on a phone) the thread hit 22em and stopped growing; the composer row below it is flex: 0 0 auto (a fixed height), and the column's default justify-content: flex-start left the leftover space sitting empty BELOW the composer instead of inside the thread -- exactly the two things the owner described: the scrollable area not filling available space, and a void under the buttons. Fix: added `.drawer-rail-sheet .drawer-rail-sheet-panel .ux-dictate-widget-thread { max-block-size: none; }` right after the existing card override in rail.css.
decision.alternative: Could have raised the 22em number instead, but that only delays the same bug at a taller phone/viewport; `none` is correct because the SHEET itself is already the real ceiling in fullscreen (the same reasoning the existing card override already uses).
